3. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the Petitioner as Plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 225 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 45 Court, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract for getting executed and registered a kabala deed against one Abu Siddique. That suit was decreed on 28.01,2001. The Petitioner started Tide Execution Case No. 01/2001. On execution of the decree he got delivery of possession in the suit land on 10.8.2004. On 11.8.2004 the Opposite Party No. 1 and 2 came up with an application under 21 Rule 99 and 100 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for getting restoration of possession in the land which was handed over in favour of the decree holder alleging inter alia that the decretal land of Title Suit No. 256 and the land upon which delivery of possession was made were not the same land. He contended that on execution of the decree the decree holder demolished his homestead and other structures and got possession upon land which was not the subject matter of the suit. The decree holder-Plaintif-Petitioner filed a Written Objection against the said application on 14.8.2004. The executing Court on hearing the learned Advocates of both the parties allowed the said prayer and directed the decree holder to hand over possession of the property in favour of the Opposite Party Nos.1 and 2 by order dated 22.8.2004. Thereafter on 24.8.2004 the present Opposite Party No.1 made another application before the executing Court for issuing a writ for restoration of possession through process of Court and the Court directed the Sheristadar to compare as to whether the decretal land and the land mentioned in the writ of delivery of possession are identical or not. The Opposite Party again filed another application on 24.8.2004 before executing Court for prosecuting the decree holder under section 195 and 1476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thereafter the executing Court by order dated 24.8.2004 issued a notice upon the decreed holder for prosecuting him for contempt of Court. On receipt of a report from Sheristadar the executing Court by order dated 26.8.2004 issued writ of delivery of possession for restoration of possession in favour of Opposite Party No.1 . 4. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 22.8.2004, 24.8.2004 and 26.8.2004 the decree holder filed a Civil Revision Under Section 115(11) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned District Judge, Dhaka and the said application was, registered as being Civil' Revision No. 415 of 2004. The learned District Judge fixed the case for hearing fixing 25.9.2004. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order the decree holder has obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr. Md. Mahmudul Hoque, the learned Advocate on appearing for the Petitioner has submitted that the orders impugned in Civil Revision No. 415 of 2004 were not passed in accordance with Order 21 Rule 100(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submitted that the learned District Judge fixed the Civil Revision No.415 of 2004 for hearing on 25.9.2004 but thereafter he transferred the said matter before the Additional District Judge beyond the knowledge of the decree holder. He submitted that the decree-holder was not at all informed the fact of transfer of the said civil revision to the 5" Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka. He submitted that the impugned orders having passed without deciding the matters in controversy on merit them has occasioned a failure of justice by the impugned orders. He prayed for interference by this Court and prayed for an appropriate order to meet the ends of justice. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Zalil Gazi, the learned Advocate on appearing for the Opposite Party on the other hand submitted that the decree holder by practicing fraud upon the Court managed to get included the homstead of the opposite party in the writ of delivery of possession, which was not the Subject of the Title Suit No. 256 of 2000. He submitted that the said matter was brought to the notice Of the Court and the Court directed the Sheristadar to submit a show cause on explaining the allegations. He submitted that on receiving the said show cause the executing Court was satisfied that fraud was committed and accordingly the writ of delivery of possession was issued by order dated 26.8.2001. He submitted that the executing Court did not commit any illegality in passing the orders dated 22.8.2004, 24.8.2004 and 26.8.2004. He submitted that those orders being lawful order, the Additional District Judge did not commit any error of law resulting in an error in the decision in 'passing the impugned order. 

 11. The orders impugned in the Civil Revision No. 415 of 2004 being the orders dated 22.8.2004, 24.8.2004 and 26.8.2004 passed by the executing Court in Title Execution Case No. 01 of 2001 allowing an application under Order 21 Rule 100 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also issuing writ of delivery of possession for restoration of possession in favour of the Opposite Party No. I to the land which was already delivered possession in favour of the Petitioner. Order 21 and Rule 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers an executing Court to restoration of possession in favour of the 3n1 person if that 3'd person is dispossessed from his lawful possession in his land. Order 21 Rule 100(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for making an investigation by the executing Court in allowing an application made under order 21 Rule 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure. For proper appreciation the provision of Order 21 Rule 100 is quoted below:" 100-(1) where any 'person other than the judgment debtor is disposed of immovable properly by the holder of the decree for the possession of such property or, where such property has been sold in execution of a decree, by the purchaser thereof, he may make an application to the Court complaining of such dispossession. "(2) The Court shall fix a day for investigating the matter and summon the party against whom the application is made to appear and answer the Same." From Order 21 Rule 100(2) it appears that the executing Court is mandatorily obliged to make an investigation into the matter to be satisfied himself that any possession of land was made over to the decree holder beyond the decretal land. It appears from the order dated 22.8.2004, 24.8.2004 and 26.8.2004 that no such investigation was made by the executing Court at the time of allowing those prayer.
